meta.defaultScope: US domestic, main-cabin economy, one-way per passenger
meta.note: Single source of truth. api/scripts/generate-seed.mjs generates api/seed.sql from this file; the frontend imports it for prerendered content pages and as an explicitly-dated offline fallback. Every record carries provenance. Records with status 'unverified' have NOT been checked against the airline source by a data steward and are surfaced in the UI as 'Review pending'.

statusValues.verified: A named data steward compared this record against source_url on verified_at.
statusValues.unverified: Value carried over from an earlier build. Source URL is recorded so it can be checked, but no steward has confirmed it.
statusValues.assumption: Not published as a single figure by the airline. PackRight applies this as a clearly-labelled planning assumption, never as a quoted price.

assumptions.label: Oversized personal item
assumptions.change_note: Placeholder retained from the initial MVP build. Airlines do not publish a single flat oversize charge for personal items; the real outcome is usually gate-checking at that airline's carry-on or checked-bag rate. Displayed as a planning assumption only.

assumptions.label: Carry-on too large at the gate
assumptions.change_note: Placeholder retained from the initial MVP build. Gate-check outcomes vary by airline, fare and airport. Displayed as a planning assumption only.

assumptions.label: Checked bag over the weight limit
assumptions.change_note: Fallback only. Airlines publish overweight charges in bands that differ per airline, and those bands are now carried on each airline record, so this assumption is applied only where an airline publishes no band for the bag in hand.

assumptions.label: Third and each additional checked bag
assumptions.change_note: Placeholder retained from the initial MVP build. Displayed as a planning assumption only.

Spirit's own baggage page states that bag prices vary by dates of travel, route and channel of purchase and sends travellers to its baggage calculator, so the carried-over 59 and 79 dollar figures - which had no source - are now left unpriced and the calculator reports them as not priced. Spirit publishes its overweight bands (41-50, 51-70 and 71-100 lb) and its oversize bands (63-80 in and over 80 in), but the amounts are produced per itinerary by that same calculator, so no band amount is recorded here. FLAGGED: Spirit's Contract of Carriage, updated 30 April 2026, defines a standard checked bag as up to 62 linear inches and 50 pounds, while the consumer baggage pages state a 40 lb limit. The 40 lb figure is kept and needs one confirmation pass on Spirit's live baggage page, which could not be opened from this network (DNS and bot protection).

Allegiant allows one free personal item that must be stored completely under the seat in front of you, one carry-on bag per passenger that must fit in the overhead bin, and up to four pre-purchased checked bags of up to 50 lb and 80 linear inches. fareFamilies.scope: US domestic, main-cabin economy, one-way, per passenger, paid at the airport (Hawaiian prints the prepaid price alongside the airport price)
fareFamilies.change_note: Main Cabin standard bag: 1st checked bag 40 USD (35 USD prepaid), 2nd 45 USD, 3rd 150 USD, 4th and each additional bag 150 USD. A carry-on bag and a personal item are included.

fareFamilies.name: Basic Economy
fareFamilies.source_title: Hawaiian Airlines - Checked baggage fees and policies
fareFamilies.scope: US domestic, main-cabin economy, one-way, per passenger, paid at the airport (Hawaiian prints the prepaid price alongside the airport price)
fareFamilies.change_note: Basic Economy standard bag: 1st checked bag 40 USD (35 USD prepaid), 2nd 45 USD, 3rd 150 USD, 4th and each additional bag 150 USD. Basic Economy does not include a full-size carry-on on most domestic routes, but a personal item is still permitted.

fareFamilies.name: Standard
fareFamilies.source_title: Allegiant Air - Carry-On and Checked Baggage Policy, Size & Fees
fareFamilies.scope: US domestic, main-cabin economy, one-way, per passenger (Allegiant prices every bag for the route and the date, and its own calculator labels its figures estimates)
fareFamilies.change_note: Allegiant publishes no fixed bag price: its own bag fee calculator produces per-route estimates and labels them as such. The base checked-bag fee and the carry-on fee are left unpriced and the calculator reports them as not priced. One personal item is included free; the carry-on and checked bags are paid add-ons.

fareFamilies.name: Standard
fareFamilies.scope: US domestic, main-cabin economy, one-way, per passenger (Breeze prices every bag for the booking session, so no single figure is published)
fareFamilies.change_note: Breeze publishes no single base bag price: its own bag pricing page states that the prices displayed apply to the current web browser session and that existing bookings should be checked through My Trips. The base checked-bag fee and the carry-on fee are left unpriced and the calculator reports them as not priced. One personal item is included free on every fare; carry-on and checked bags are sold separately or in bundles.

fareFamilies.name: Standard
fareFamilies.scope: US domestic, main-cabin economy, one-way, per passenger (Avelo publishes a "from" price that rises with the route and the time of purchase)
fareFamilies.change_note: Avelo charges a flat price per bag, "from $49 to $75" for a checked bag and "from $54 to $75" for the overhead carry-on, so the lowest published figure is recorded for each. Up to ten checked bags may be bought per traveller, each at the same per-bag price. One personal item is included free; the carry-on and checked bags are paid add-ons, and pre-paying costs less.
